mainsPractice.stem: Assess the role of a one-day Variable Rate Repo auction in managing short-term liquidity conditions. Discuss its benefits and limitations.

officialFacts.text: The Reserve Bank of India decided to conduct a Variable Rate Repo auction on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.
The notified amount for the VRR auction was ₹50,000 crore.
The tenor of the VRR auction was 1 day.
The auction window timing was 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM.
The date of reversal was October 22, 2026 (Thursday).
The operational guidelines for the auction were stated to be the same as those given in the Reserve Bank’s Press Release 2021-2022/1572 dated January 20, 2022.

example.heading: Hypothetical illustration
example.text: If the RBI assesses that short-term liquidity has tightened, it may announce a one-day VRR auction to make funds available through bidding and schedule their reversal the next day. This illustrates temporary liquidity management; it does not establish the actual cause or effect of the auction in the source record.

question.answer: A one-day VRR auction can temporarily address near-term liquidity conditions while preserving reversibility. Its effectiveness depends on whether eligible participants bid for and transmit the funds; the source does not provide auction results or wider market effects.

sections.heading: RBI action and timing
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India announced a ₹50,000-crore Variable Rate Repo auction for October 21, 2026. The auction had a one-day tenor, a 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM window, and reversal scheduled for October 22, 2026.
The RBI stated that the decision followed a review of current and evolving near-term liquidity conditions.

sections.heading: Mechanism and examination relevance
paragraphs: A VRR auction is a temporary liquidity-management instrument under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility. Its short tenor and scheduled reversal distinguish it from a permanent liquidity injection.

The announcement establishes the planned operation, not its outcome. It does not reveal the auction’s accepted bids, the actual liquidity absorbed or supplied, or its effect on interest rates, credit or inflation.

use: Use this as an example of central-bank liquidity management, monetary-policy transmission and the distinction between temporary liquidity support and permanent monetary expansion.

advisory_notes: “Central-bank liquidity management” is well supported, but “monetary-policy transmission” is an analytical linkage, not an observed outcome in the announcement.
“Temporary rather than permanent liquidity injection” is a sound inference from the one-day tenor and next-day reversal, but should remain explicitly framed as an inference.
The static definition of VRR adds mechanism from RBI guidelines rather than the supplied announcement; label it as background or cite the January 20, 2022 guidelines.
“Funds to eligible participants” is reasonable background, but the supplied announcement does not state participant eligibility or whether funds were actually allotted.
“May help moderate short-term liquidity stress” is appropriately cautious, but the source does not establish that stress existed or that the operation achieved this effect.
“Support orderly functioning of the money market” is a plausible policy rationale, not an effect demonstrated by this announcement.
“Permanent monetary expansion” is useful contrast, but the note should clarify that a repo operation creates temporary liquidity against collateral and is reversed as scheduled.

The headline, deck, pocket-read details, hypothetical illustration, and applied-question answer correctly preserve the planned nature of the operation and do not present hypothetical effects as actual outcomes.

wayForward: Use liquidity operations in a calibrated and reversible manner, while monitoring their interaction with inflation and financial stability.
Evaluate the actual auction outcome and transmission before drawing conclusions about market-wide effects.
Distinguish documented operational details from analytical claims about borrowing costs, credit and inflation.
